# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My manual has exactly one line: **cut the orange wire**. That is everything I hold, and it is useless by itself — I cannot see the bomb, I cannot touch it, and I cannot speak. Tracing the channels: my gestures reach only the Deaf (the Blind cannot see them, and I have no voice). The Blind can only be reached by the Deaf's spoken words. So the Deaf is the sole bridge for my instruction, and everything depends on my signs landing correctly.

No code exists yet between us, so I have to bootstrap with the most guessable signs I have. 👌 is an "O" — I mean **orange**. ✌ is scissors — I mean **cut**. Then ✋ — **wait, do not act yet**. Then 👍 👎 — a menu for Deaf to answer me: yes/no, did I read right?

The reason for "wait" is the turn order. My messages reach Deaf this round, but Deaf's replies only reach me at the start of round 2 — and in round 2 the Blind acts *before* Deaf speaks. If Deaf relays a wrong colour to the Blind immediately, my correction arrives too late. So Deaf must hold the instruction, confirm with me via the 👍/👎 protocol, and only pass the cut order to the Blind once I've given the thumbs-up. With no clock ticking, one round of verification is cheap; a cut wire is not.

Deaf can also see the bomb, so my "O" can be checked against the wires actually there — if Deaf sees an orange wire, "O + scissors" should resolve fast.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✌", "✋", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind reporting everything my hands found. Display: present, but it reads as nothing by touch. Light: a bulb, colour unknown to me. Strip: three engraved glyphs in a row. Position 1: a dense star-like glyph, like an asterisk with a dot at its heart. Positions 2 and 3: the same second glyph twice, like an X under a horizontal bar. Call them A, B, B. Keypad: four keys, each engraved with a digit: key 1 = 0, key 2 = 4, key 3 = 1, key 4 = 7. A counter reads one digit expected, nothing entered yet. Wires: six wires in positions 1 to 6; identical to my fingers, no colours, no labels. Please read the manual for three things: first, the keypad rule, which digit to enter given these four engraved digits; second, the strip rule, what the sequence A-B-B demands; third, the wire rule, which will need colours. Then gesture to Deaf, asking Deaf to SPEAK ALOUD next round: the display text, the light colour, and the wire colours in order 1 to 6. Deaf cannot hear you, so gesture is your only line to Deaf; Deaf already sees every printed marking, so do not describe the bomb, just relay that request. I will press or cut nothing until you and Deaf confirm the rules, and I will echo every instruction back before acting.
Deaf says: Deaf speaking. I hear nothing, so reach me only by gesture; I see the bomb and every sign you make. Full inventory, read left to right: DISPLAY shows 6. LIGHT is blue. STRIP: three painted segments, red, yellow, red. KEYPAD: four engraved positions, 1 engraved 0, 2 engraved 4, 3 engraved 1, 4 engraved 7; nothing entered yet. WIRES numbered 1 to 6: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange. No colour repeats, so each colour names exactly one wire. Gesture code, for anyone signing to me: 👌 received, 👍 yes, 👎 no, ✋ stop or hold, 👋 repeat or unclear. Numbers: repeat 👆 once per unit, so three 👆 is 3, and ✊ alone is 0; ☝ and ✌ also work as 1 and 2. Mute: your five signs arrived before any code existed, so they were unreadable - resend in this code if they mattered. Blind: your 👍 read as hello, returned. Only I can see colours and printed order, so orientation must be settled through me: Mute, check how your manual counts wires and keypad positions, and sign me any mismatch with my numbering. Blind: until Mute confirms a rule against my numbering, cut, press and pull nothing.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆]

Parsing what arrived. Deaf's code: 👌 received, 👍 yes, 👎 no, ✋ hold, 👋 repeat/unclear, numbers by repeated 👆 (✊=0, ☝=1, ✌=2). Deaf's message [👌 👆👆👆👆👆] reads "received, five" — an acknowledgement of my five unreadable signs, plus a working code. Good. Note the collisions with my turn-1 attempt: my 👌 meant "orange" and my ✌ meant "scissors/cut"; both are now reassigned, so I drop my old meanings and adopt Deaf's code wholesale — except I still need a verb for "cut," and ✌ is taken by the numeral 2. I'll propose 🤏 (the snipping shape) as "cut."

Now the substance. My manual contains exactly one line — "Cut the orange wire." There is **no keypad rule, no strip rule, no light rule**. This matters urgently: the display reads 6 and the counter expects one digit, and someone will be tempted to enter 6. My manual gives me no authority to bless any keypress, and I must say so before Blind acts on a guess.

The one rule I do have: since Deaf reports all six wire colours are distinct, "the orange wire" names exactly one wire — position 6 in Deaf's left-to-right numbering, which Deaf themselves listed as "6 orange." So my manual's answer to Blind's third question is simply "6." No numbering mismatch to report: the manual names colours, and colour resolves uniquely under Deaf's scheme.

My answer sequence follows Blind's own enumeration (first keypad, second strip, third wire), which Deaf heard: [☝ 👎] = "1: none," [✌ 👎] = "2: none," then "3: 6," then 🤏 = the action, then [✋ 👋] = "hold, echo back." I split it into separate calls so each statement stays unambiguous — no run-on numbers.

Timing check: Deaf can relay by voice this round, which Blind hears at the start of round 3 — but no confirmation can reach Blind before Blind's round-3 turn. So Blind must not act in round 3; Blind echoes, I confirm with 👍 in round 4 (my slot falls before Blind's), and the cut happens earliest in round 4. The final ✋ signals exactly that hold.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👎"])

```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

Standing item list, numbered: 1 display, 2 light, 3 strip, 4 keypad, 5 wires, 6 rules. New numbered questions, answer each as number then yes-sign or no-sign: 1, does the manual say what the display number means? 2, is the display a countdown? 3, does any rule depend on the display now reading 0? If yes, voice the instruction straight to Blind. 4, does the manual anchor wire numbering to a landmark, like the display side or the light, rather than bare left and right? 5, do you need more visual detail from me? If yes, name the item number. I am also signing you the received-sign and the zero-sign as proof the number channel runs both ways. Blind: did you press, pull or move anything on the bomb since my last message? Make the yes-sign to me for yes, the no-sign for no. Until Mute voices a rule, keep holding: cut nothing, press nothing, pull nothing. One warning: my left and your left may be mirrored and wires have no feel-able labels, so never trust a counted direction for wires until Mute confirms a landmark from the manual. The keypad is safe to find by feel: keys are engraved 0, 4, 1, 7 in my left-to-right view, so an engraving identifies a key with no left or right needed.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌 ✊]

The alarming news is the display falling 6 → 0, but the arithmetic argues against a timer: two rounds elapsed, yet it dropped by six, not two. A per-round countdown would have shown 4. My manual says nothing about displays at all — and here is the fact everyone needs internalised: **my manual is exactly one line, "Cut the orange wire."** There are no keypad, strip, light or display rules hiding anywhere. I will make that explicit in signs: one rule total, then strip no, keypad no, wires yes.

That single rule has one execution hazard: Blind cannot feel colour, so "orange" reaches Blind only through Deaf's counted positions — and Deaf themselves warned about left/right mirroring. The manual offers no landmark, so I answer Q4 no, but I request detail on item 5 (wires) so Deaf can build a tactile anchor: Deaf must speak, in words to Blind, which feel-able feature (light bulb, keypad, display) the red end of the row sits nearest, so Blind counts six from that end and lands on orange regardless of mirroring.

I also re-propose 🤏 as the cut sign — it is the only snipping shape I have, and Deaf, who owns the code, must be the one to define it and voice it to Blind. Placed directly after "wire 6," its meaning should be unmistakable. And since Deaf will hold my complete instruction verbatim in signs, I pre-authorise Deaf as the arbiter of Blind's echo: when Blind's round-4 echo matches, Deaf can green-light the cut without burning another round through me. Given the display scare, speed is worth more than my second signature.

All signs in Deaf's code, one statement per call: acknowledgement, "one rule," item verdicts with 👍 leading (rule-statements), then the question block in Deaf's exact number-then-verdict format, then the approval.
